Where this can flex

The buy is deliberately lean, just the airport board and the truck. Two fixed boards sit in Good to have if we want more coverage: the downtown Sheraton board at $1,500 for the week reads the hotel blocks all week rather than one evening pass, and the inbound I-70 board at $1,375 picks up the highway itself, which the truck legally cannot run. Easy to add either back, and just as easy to leave out.

The recommended buy

Two placements, kept deliberately simple. The airport board carries the full week and catches every fan flying in. The truck handles everything else, running the surface approaches through Morrison on show days, then swinging downtown to the Sheraton and 16th Street at night. Since the truck covers the venue drive and the hotel blocks itself, a separate downtown or Red Rocks board is not needed in the core buy, though the downtown board sits in Good to have to add back if we want a fixed presence all week. Worth knowing that LED trucks cannot advertise on interstates, confirmed independently by two operators, so the truck runs the approach roads rather than I-70 itself.

Mobile LED, the vendor field

Six operators quoted on an identical scope of one truck running 12-hour days, so the numbers compare cleanly. Lime is the recommendation. Bulldog came in lowest and Mobile Impact is a hair cheaper per day, but the spread across two days is small enough that what each vendor includes matters more than the headline number.
Routing, what is confirmed and what is not

LED trucks are not permitted to advertise on interstate highways. Advanced Mobile LED and Can't Miss US said so independently, so running I-70 itself is out for a moving truck. Trucks can drive the interstate to reposition with the screens dark, then run screens-on along the surface approaches. The venue is reached from I-70 Exit 259 onto Morrison Road and then W Alameda Pkwy, with a second approach from C-470 at the Morrison exit and an overflow route via US-285 and Highway 8. Because that final access road runs a single lane, sold-out traffic crawls, so the creative holds the same audience for minutes instead of seconds. Evenings shift downtown to the Sheraton and the blocks bracketing 16th Street, which every operator confirmed is clear. Two things are not yet settled. Running inside the Red Rocks parking lots would need permission from the venue, since the park is Denver city land, and Omid already flagged that as something to check rather than assume. Separately, silent visual means the screens carry no audio, which is standard across the field, but it does not make the vehicle itself quiet. Only Mobile Impact's all-electric solar truck is mechanically silent, which is the one that genuinely suits the residential stretch through Morrison.

Why Lime over the cheaper quotes

Mobile Impact is marginally cheaper at $2,000 a day against Lime's $2,025, which works out to $50 across the two show days. That gap is not worth much. Lime is the more established operation, they own and build everything in house, and their quote already carries the activation manager, the custom route, and the client portal with live tracking and all the POP photos, so we know there are no costs waiting for us later. We also have room to push on price, since it looks like we will be doing recurring business with them across other projects, and that is a conversation worth having before we sign anything.

Closest to the venue, most likely unavailable

These are the absolute closest boards to the venue, shown for completeness, but realistically out of reach for this window. The two literal closest sit right at the Morrison exit, about 2.2 miles out, but they are older non-conforming structures and the state only lists an out-of-state landowner. The current ads on them are Outcrop Red Rocks and Alchemy, so I am reaching out to those brands to find who they bought the space from and run down the actual owner. The other two are the south-facing faces of OUTFRONT's I-70 cluster, which read the wrong direction for inbound show traffic, so they are not part of the plan. The one face in that cluster worth having, the north-side board Chase is holding at $3,000, is up in Good to have. Nothing in the state list sits closer than about two miles, since Morrison is a protected scenic area.
